rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Charging a capacitor stores energy in its electric field: integrating the charging work gives $U = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = \frac{1}{2}QV = \frac{Q^2}{2C}$ — the ½ because the average charging voltage is V/2. NEB 2022's 6 μF at 100 V stores 0.03 J (3m); NEB 2024's 12 μF at 100 V stores 0.06 J (2m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C - Energy density: u = ½ε₀E²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **The ½ is real:** U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C — three equivalent forms.  ·  **Energy sits in the field**, not "on the plates" — density ½ε₀E².

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A sketched sign convention is part of the data.  ·  A dimensionless ratio still needs the two quantities named.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: energy of charged capacitor (within Capacitor).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Copy the worked example and hide the result until the last step.  ·  Name the unit of every term in the formula.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "U = ½ × μF × V² — watch the exponents."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find the energy in a 100 μF capacitor at 50 V.** — U = ½ × 10⁻⁴ × 2500 = 0.125 J.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote all three equivalent forms; the derivation from Q–V area earns full marks.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Energy Held in Empty Space A charged capacitor stores energy in the electric field between its plates — no moving parts, no chemistry. Discharge it through a flash lamp or a defibrillator and the field's work arrives in a burst. U = ½CV² is the formula NEB keeps testing.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Deriving the stored energy Charging a capacitor is a gradual process: when charge q has been transferred, the remaining work pushes charge against potential v = q/C.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 90:** U = ½QV is the area under the charging curve — potential energy language. - **To Topic 93/94:** C sets the storage capacity. - **To fields:** energy density ½ε₀E² makes field energy a real, localised physical quantity.
